title: Concept: eval() as a code sink
description: eval() compiles a string at run time, so the executed code is whatever that string holds; if any part is attacker-influenced the result is code execution with the application's privileges. Even static strings are opaque to review and to Content-Security-Policy.
applicability: JavaScript and TypeScript source, including JSX and TSX components.
risk: Arbitrary code execution in the page or runtime context; MEDIUM severity pending review of the argument's provenance.
